title: Long-term support channel and compatibility enforcement
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Define and implement a Long-Term Support (LTS) channel design and an automated compatibility/support matrix across the serving runtime, public API, official SDKs (Python, Node), and Redwood Console. Goal is to give customers a clear, machine-readable compatibility promise and enforcement paths to avoid silent breakage during upgrades and rollouts.
notes_or_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff meeting with Product (Maya), SRE (Jordan), and Design (Leo). Agreed scope: runtime + API + SDKs + Console; exclude third-party client libraries for now.

2026-03-11: Drafted initial compatibility principles in Confluence: semantic stability for minor/patch, explicit cross-component version mapping for major changes, 12-month LTS windows, and 90-day deprecation notices.

2026-03-11: Engineering design review: two trade-offs surfaced — strict enforcement (reject incompatible clients) vs soft-warning mode. Decided to target enforcement for runtime<->API pairing, soft-warning for SDK<->Console on first rollout. Will iterate after customer beta.

2026-03-12: PoC started for an enforcement service that consults a centralized JSON support matrix (github.com/redwood-inference/release-matrix repo, PR #537). PoC validates runtime binary "compat_tag" against API accepted pairs and emits telemetry to rollout dashboard.
acceptance_criteria: A machine-readable support matrix (JSON) exists in the release-matrix repo and is versioned with tags
Runtime rejects API requests when incompatible according to matrix (enforcement mode) and emits clear error code + mitigation instruction
SDKs surface deprecation warnings when used with API/runtime versions outside supported range
Console shows per-customer view of active runtime/API/SDK versions and highlights customers impacted by planned rollouts
Rollout gate integrations: canary gate checks matrix compatibility and blocks rollout if high-risk mismatches detected
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Customers running older SDKs may receive hard failures if enforcement is too strict. Mitigation: default enforcement=soft for SDKs for first 30 days and provide migration guidance and compatibility shim.
Risk: Matrix drift (owners forget to update). Mitigation: CI gate that requires matrix update for breaking PRs and owner labels assigned per component.
Risk: Increased operational complexity during rollouts. Mitigation: add per-rollout simulation step that verifies customer fleets against matrix within the console before activating rollout gates.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (Beta, 4 weeks): Publish support matrix format; PoC enforcement for runtime<->API in staging; generate SDK warning hooks.
Phase 2 (Customer beta, 8 weeks): Invite top 5 customers to opt-in to enforcement; collect telemetry and false-positive reports; iterate matrix schema.
Phase 3 (GA, 12 weeks): Enable enforcement for all managed customers for runtime<->API; Console rollout gates enabled; SDK defaults remain in soft-warning for one release cycle.
Rollback approach: gate can be flipped to permissive mode and a hotfix matrix deployed; emergency telemetry alert to SRE channel and automated rollback of rollout if >5% error spike.
